# `spell/known-typo-key`

**No known typos in keys, classes and ids**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-spell` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-spell` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JSON, YAML, TOML, CSS, SCSS, HTML |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:spell/recommended` at `warn` · `codelaw:spell/strict` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (other files read the name — the code that reads a key, the markup that uses a class, the link to an id — so renaming it here alone breaks them) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.3.0 |

## What it checks

A name other files read holds a word on the pack's list of known typos: a JSON, YAML or TOML key, a CSS or SCSS class, id, custom property, `$variable`, mixin or function, or an HTML `id`. The name is split at case changes, `_`, `-`, `.` and digits, and each part of four letters or more is looked up. Each distinct name is reported once per file, where it is first declared.

**Why:** a misspelled key or class is copied into every file that reads it, and `grep receive` never finds it. It is cheapest to fix before it has readers, and it is never safe to fix in one file alone.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-spell
pip install codelaw-rules-spell
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:spell/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:spell/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"spell/known-typo-key" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.json"]
rules = { "spell/known-typo-key" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"spell/known-typo-key" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"spell/known-typo-key" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"spell/known-typo-key" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "spell/known-typo-key": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JSON** has no comments: switch the rule off for the file with a scope, or use the baseline.
- **YAML:** `# codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key: <reason>`
- **CSS:** `/* codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key: <reason> */`
- **SCSS:** `// codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key: <reason>`
- **HTML:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key: <reason> -->`
- **Dated:** `# codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule spell/known-typo-key --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain spell/known-typo-key       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule spell/known-typo-key  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>        # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Find every reader of the name: search the project for it (`git grep -n recieve_all`), including code that builds it from parts.
2. Rename it here and in every reader in one change; for a key or class published to other projects, accept both names for a release before removing the old one.
3. For a name that is right as it stands (a field another system defines), excuse the line: `# codelaw-ignore spell/known-typo-key: <reason>`.

## Examples

### JSON

#### Don't

```json
{ "recieveTimeout": 30 }
```

#### Do

```json
{ "receiveTimeout": 30 }
```

### YAML

#### Don't

```yaml
recieve_timeout: 30
```

#### Do

```yaml
receive_timeout: 30
```

### TOML

#### Don't

```toml
[server]
recieve_timeout = 30
```

#### Do

```toml
[server]
receive_timeout = 30
```

### CSS

#### Don't

```css
.adress-card { padding: 1rem; }
```

#### Do

```css
.address-card { padding: 1rem; }
```

### SCSS

#### Don't

```scss
$line-lenght: 70ch;
```

#### Do

```scss
$line-length: 70ch;
```

### HTML

#### Don't

```html
<section id="adress-form"></section>
```

#### Do

```html
<section id="address-form"></section>
```
